job.title: Internal Communications Executive (Higher Executive Officer)
job.description:
Key Details:

Location: Dublin HQ or a regional office (by agreement), with a nationwide remit

Contract: Full-time, permanent

Salary: €60,029 – €76,546 (starting at the first point of the scale)

Closing date: Thursday 15 October 2026 at 5pm


HSA Brochure HEO Communications Executive.pdf

Internal Communications Executive - Application Form.docx


About the HSA

The Health and Safety Authority is Ireland's national body for workplace safety, health and welfare. It regulates and promotes safe working lives, oversees the safe use and transport of chemicals, and acts as Ireland's national accreditation body through INAB. With a presence in every county and a voice in European and international forums, the HSA's vision is simple: to deliver healthy and safe working lives and contribute to productive enterprises.


About the role

This is a chance to shape how a national regulator talks to its own people. Reporting to the Head of Communications and Customer Relations, you'll lead the delivery of a high-impact internal communications plan that supports performance, strengthens culture and helps the HSA deliver its statutory mandate.

You'll turn strategy, regulatory priorities and operational plans into clear, engaging messages that staff actually want to read, and you'll help managers across the organisation communicate well too.


What you'll be doing


The following is a non-exhaustive list of key accountabilities that are typically allocated, but are not limited to, the role:

  • Develop, implement and continuously review processes and procedures to support effectiveinternal communication.
  • Work with senior management to deliver an organisation-wide internal communications planthat delivers key messages at key stages, tosupport the HSA’s Strategy Statement,Programmes of Work, Executive Team priorities,organisational culture, and public sectorgovernance and accountability requirements.
  • Based on agreed priorities, translate organisational strategy, regulatory priorities and operational initiatives into clear, accessible and staff-relevant messaging.
  • Ensure internal communications reinforce the HSA’s vision and values.
  • Ensure strong coordination between the internal communications role, senior management and operational divisions.
  • Oversee and continuously improve the HSA’sinternal communications channels, including:
  • Staff intranet (eXchange)
  • Webinars
  • Leadership updates and internal meetings
  • Internal publications and digital content
  • Ensure all content is clear, consistent, accessible and aligned with HSA brand and accessibility requirements.
  • Provide guidance and support to managers across the organisation in planning and delivering effective internal communications.
  • Build strong working relationships across divisions to ensure coordinated and aligned messaging.
  • Lead internal communications for key organisational initiatives, including:
  • Strategy development
  • Culture and engagement programmes
  • HR and wellbeing initiatives(in partnership with HR)
  • Organisational change and transformation programmes
  • Support as required the delivery of internal campaigns that drive awareness, engagement and behavioural change.
  • Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of internal communications using feedback and performance data, where available.
  • Provide insights and recommendations to improve communication effectiveness and staff engagement.
  • Identify and implement new tools, platforms, and approaches to enhance internal communications effectiveness.
  • Promote best practice in internal communications across the organisation through guidance,templates, and training.
  • Support internal communications during incidents or critical events to ensure staff are informed in a timely and accurate manner.
  • Ensure alignment between internal and external messaging during high-profile or sensitive issues.


What you'll need (essential)

  • A Level 7 qualification (or higher) in a relevant discipline
  • At least three years' experience in an internal communications role
  • A track record of working with senior managers to deliver successful internal comms outcomes
  • Excellent writing and editing skills, with the ability to make complex information clear and engaging
  • Experience using internal comms channels and tools such as intranet, email, webinars, staff events or digital content platforms


It would be great if you also have (desirable)

  • Experience supporting culture, engagement or organisational change
  • Experience in a public sector, regulatory or complex stakeholder environment
  • Knowledge of accessibility, plain English and inclusive communications principles


What's on offer

  • Permanent public service role (subject to a nine-month probation)
  • Salary scale of €60,029 – €76,546, with long service increments available
  • 29 days' annual leave, rising to 30 after five years
  • Blended working and a range of work-life balance options
  • Public service pension (Single Public Service Pension Scheme)
  • Cycle to Work and Tax Saver schemes
  • Staff wellbeing programme, including an Employee Assistance Programme and health screening
  • Ongoing learning and development, including a Refund of Fees Scheme for further education


Please note: the starting salary is at the minimum point of the scale and isn't negotiable. Different pay and conditions may apply to serving civil or public servants.


How to apply

Internal Communications Executive - Application Form.docx

HSA Brochure HEO Communications Executive.pdf


Recruitment for this role is managed by Conscia on behalf of the HSA.

Download the Candidate Information Booklet and Application Form. Complete the form and submit it by clicking "Apply for Job"

CVs and cover letters are not required and should not be submitted. Shortlisting is based entirely on your application form, so give a full and detailed account of how your skills and experience match the requirements.

You'll receive an acknowledgement email once your application is received. If you don't hear back within two working days, contact hsa@consciatalent.com.


Closing date: Thursday 15 October 2026 at 5pm. Late applications can't be accepted.


Selection process

The process may include shortlisting, interviews, online testing, written or work-sample exercises and a presentation. Successful candidates will be placed on a panel (valid for 12 months) from which roles will be offered in order of merit.


The HSA is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds. Reasonable accommodations are available for candidates with disabilities. Please note that canvassing will lead to disqualification.

The Health and Safety Authority (HSA) are recruiting Grade II Inspectors across a number of their Teams; Agriculture, Utilities, Manufacturing and Investigation Unit, to help them do what they do best - making a difference to workers across Ireland by keeping them safe and protected.



Key Responsibilities:

The following non-exhaustive list of tasks are those that a Grade II Inspector could be assigned. Please note that the final set of tasks will reflect the role the person is offered:

  • Carries out inspections, market surveillance and investigations within relevant area and inputs these into Platform(s) in accordance with their Programme of Work.
  • Prepares and delivers reports and updates to the relevant manager on the performance of the team and highlights any corrective actions taken to address issues of concern.

Reviews and prepares technical assessments and reports in line with legislative requirements.

In addition to demonstrating that you possess the required competencies, the ideal candidate must be able to demonstrate:

  • Primary degree (NFQ level 8 or equivalent) Engineering, Science, Occupational Health and Safety, Agricultural Science, Operations Management or other appropriate discipline.

Desirable Requirements:

  • Experience in the management of staff.

job.description:
Candidate Information Booklet - FSPO AP RER Sept.pdf


Application Form - Registration and Early Resolution Senior Manager.docx


About the Role

Reporting to the Director of Registration, Early Resolution and Transformation, the Registration and Early Resolution Senior Managers are responsible for planning and managing team capacity, monitoring performance, identifying operational risks and bottlenecks, driving service improvement initiatives and using management information to support effective decision-making. The postholders also contribute to cross-organisational projects, policy development and change initiatives, particularly where these affect complaint intake, assessment processes, mediation or other dispute resolution services, quality standards, staff capability and customer experience. 


Key Responsibilities:

  • Leading the day-to-day operation of a functional team in the Registration & Customer Experience, Early Jurisdictional Assessment, or Dispute Resolution (mediation) sections within the Registration and Early Resolution directorate, to ensure the timely and effective management of high-volume caseloads; 
  • Managing complaint registration, assessment, jurisdictional and compliance assessments, and associated workflow decisions in line with legislation, policy and procedure; 
  • Managing a functional Dispute Resolution (Mediation) team and service, ensuring that we deliver high quality, impartial and timely mediation (or other dispute resolution) services that maximise the FSPO’s impact on the resolution of complaints, while providing high levels of customer satisfaction; 
  • Further evolving the dispute resolution service to maximise complaint resolutions by informal means, including by contribution to (and support of) a robust training programme for mediators, conciliators and other team members, as required; 
  • Ensuring robust quality assurance arrangements are in place so that decisions, correspondence, records and process outputs are accurate, consistent and of a high standard; 
  • Driving high standards of customer service, including the management of sensitive and complex interactions with complainants, providers and representatives; 
  • Leading, motivating and developing staff, including work allocation, performance management, coaching, attendance management and supporting staff wellbeing; 
  • Using data and management information to monitor throughput, trends, risks, service levels and team performance, and taking appropriate action to address issues; 
  • Working collaboratively with internal stakeholders to support service integration, process improvement, digital transformation and organisational change; 
  • Ensuring compliance with governance requirements, risk controls, data protection obligations and internal policies; and 
  • Contributing to the achievement of organisational objectives through active participation in projects, reporting, planning and strategic initiatives. 



Essential Requirements:

Candidates must, on or before Friday 2 October 2026, meet the following requirements:


  • A minimum of 3 years’ direct team management experience in a high-volume operational environment in complaint handling, case intake / registration / assessment, compliance checking, customer operations, dispute resolution, adjudicative support, regulatory administration, or a comparable service environment. 
  • Relevant experience working in a regulatory, ombudsman, legal or complaints resolution environment, in another ombudsman or Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) scheme, or in the financial services, pensions or other public sector environment; 
  • Demonstrated experience of leading and managing people, including work planning, performance management, staff development, employee engagement and the management of competing priorities; 
  • Strong evidence of sound judgement, decision-making and problem-solving, including the ability to assess issues, apply policy or legislative requirements and make balanced, well-reasoned decisions; 
  • Experience of analysing operational data and management information to monitor performance, identify risks or trends, and improve service delivery and throughput; 
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage effectively and professionally with internal and external stakeholders, including in sensitive or challenging situations; and 
  • A clear understanding of the values and responsibilities of public service, including governance, accountability, fairness, confidentiality and customer service. 



Desirable Criteria:

In addition to the essential requirements, it would be an advantage for candidates to demonstrate one or more of the following: 


  • A recognised qualification of at least NFQ Level 7 or higher in management, public administration, law, business, governance, quality assurance, customer service, human rights or a related discipline. 
  • Experience of overseeing registration, triage, admissibility, jurisdictional assessment or early resolution processes. 
  • Experience of operating in a governance-rich environment with responsibility for compliance, audit readiness, records management or risk controls. 
  • Demonstrated ability to lead change, improve processes and contribute to organisational or service development initiatives. 
  • Experience of developing and implementing quality assurance frameworks, standard operating procedures, service standards or performance dashboards. 
  • Experience of leading service improvement, digital change in an operational setting. 
  • Knowledge of administrative law, fair procedures, complaint resolution processes or relevant legislative and regulatory frameworks. 


How to Apply:

Completed application forms must be uploaded via the portal at https://www.consciatalent.com/fspo no later than 5pm (Irish time) on Friday 2nd October 2026.


Applications will not be accepted by any other method, nor if received after the closing date. CV's will not be considered.


When outlining your application, accuracy is essential. The information you supply in your application will play a central part of the selection process.


If you do not receive an acknowledgement of receipt of your application within 24 hours, please check your junk/spam folders as email notifications may be filtered here.


The onus is on each applicant to ensure that they are in receipt of all communication from Conscia Limited. Conscia Limited accept no responsibility for communication not accessed or received by an applicant.  


If you have any queries about the role, please contact us at fspo@consciatalent.com

The SFPA is seeking a Senior Port Officer  to join its established team in Howth and play a key role within the Authority,


The Senior Port Officer plays a key leadership role in ensuring the effective delivery of SFPA’s sea-fisheries control and food safety functions at port level. Based in Howth, the role carries significant responsibility for operational management, regulatory compliance, data integrity and the delivery of SFPA’s statutory objectives.


Key Responsibilities

The successful candidate will take a lead role in:

• The day-to-day operational management and coordination of local Operational matters.

• The efficient and effective performance of the Authority’s Sea-Fisheries Operations programme (Fisheries Control and Food Safety) objectives and outputs within the terms of the Authority’s Strategy and Annual Business Plan.

• To be accountable for, manage and oversee the efficient and effective collection of fish catch and fishing effort statistics for quota, effort management and policy purposes.

• Reporting to and advising the Authority on operational matters and the delivery of SFPA’s objectives.

• The implementation of all relevant EU and National legislation in relation to Food Safety and Fisheries Control and Conservation.

• The collection, collation and checking of all fish catch statistics including data gathered from EU fishing logbooks, sales notes and other data sources.

• Ensuring that the contractual commitments and responsibilities of the SFPA to the Food Safety Authority of Ireland are met and delivered.

• Supporting the EU missions on Fisheries Conservation and Control and Food Safety in your area.

• Enforcing all relevant present and future EU and National legislation in relation to Food Safety and Fisheries Control and 

Conservation.

• Acting as an authorised officer for the purposes of exercising all the powers available to authorised officers under the Food Safety Authority of Ireland Act 1998.


About the Ideal Candidate

Essential Criteria

• Minimum qualification of a National Diploma level 7 in a relevant discipline (e.g. fisheries technology, engineering, science, geography, legal, financial).

• 2 years relevant experience as a Sea Fisheries Protection Officer/ Sea Fishery Officer.

• Proven leadership and motivation skills together with the ability to allocate work to team members, set performance standards, evaluate work outputs from the team and address any issues of underperformance arising in relation to staff 

reporting directly to you.

• Strong management capability particularly in relation to managing and monitoring the delivery of the Authority’s key business objectives and regulatory responsibilities in the areas of Sea Fisheries Operations.

• Possess good communication skills particularly to act as a communicator between staff and management, keeping both well informed and up to date. 

• Proven capabilities to master, manage, and deliver a complex range of specialised technical programmes and legal issues.

• Possess good administrative capabilities, including effective report writing, work programming/planning, budget management and the use of Information Technology as a communications and monitoring tool. 

• Travel nationally and some international travel is an essential requirement of the role.

• Must hold and maintain a clean driving licence.

job.description:
Operations Delivery Manager Candidate Information Booklet.pdf

About The Role


The Institute of Public Administration (IPA) is seeking an experienced and strategic Operations Delivery Manager to lead the operational delivery of Digital Learning services and support the next phase of growth across the public service.


This role is being recruited at a pivotal stage in the evolution of the Digital Learning function. A key pillar of the IPA's strategy is the development of a shared Digital Learning Ecosystem that enables high-quality learning to operate effectively at scale across Ireland's Public Service. The introduction of a new Learning Experience Platform (LXP) in 2027 will provide the foundation for this growth, supporting the expansion of Digital Learning services from approximately 50,000 Civil Service learners to a wider Public Service audience of more than 110,000 learners by 2030. The postholder will play a leading role in implementing the new Digital Learning operating model, supporting the rollout of the Learning Experience Platform and establishing the operational structures, processes and supplier arrangements required to support future growth.


The postholder will lead the operations function, managing the Service Delivery Supervisor and wider operations team to ensure the effective delivery, continuous improvement and future scalability of Digital Learning services, comprising instructor led delivery and self-paced learning. While initially reporting to the Director of Digital Learning, the department may evolve over time to support operational leadership across the IPA as organisational structures and service models develop.


Key Responsibilities


1.      Service Performance & Delivery

 

·      Lead the Digital Learning Operations function, ensuring services are delivered efficiently, effectively and in line with agreed service standards.


·      Oversee demand forecasting, capacity planning and operational planning activities to ensure service capacity and delivery models support current and future organisational needs.


·      Establish and maintain the operational frameworks, performance measures and service standards required to support effective, scalable and high-quality service delivery.


·      Monitor service performance, quality and operational risks, using data, stakeholder feedback and performance insights to drive continuous improvement and corrective action where required.

 

2.      Supplier & Commercial Management

 

·      Define operational requirements, service standards, implementation requirements and performance measures for delivery partners, and support procurement and supplier selection activities.


·      Lead the mobilisation and implementation of new delivery partnerships, ensuring services transition smoothly into operation.


·      Build effective supplier partnerships and governance arrangements that drive high performance, continuous improvement and value for money.


·      Monitor supplier performance against contractual obligations and agreed service standards, ensuring issues are addressed and performance improvements delivered.


·      Monitor service utilisation, income and expenditure against operational and contractual targets, providing analysis, forecasting and recommendations to support effective service planning and financial performance.

 

3.      Stakeholder Management

 

·      Develop and maintain effective relationships with client organisations, ensuring a high-quality, responsive service that meets agreed expectations and supports positive customer experiences.


·      Act as a senior escalation point for operational and service delivery matters, working with stakeholders, suppliers and internal teams to resolve issues and maintain service performance.


·      Build productive partnerships with internal colleagues, training providers and public service organisations to support the effective delivery and continuous improvement of Digital Learning services.


·      Support client onboarding and service transition activities, ensuring new organisations can successfully access and adopt Digital Learning services.

 

4.      Leadership and Team Management

 

·      Lead and develop the Operations function, ensuring it has the capability, capacity and culture required to deliver high-quality services and support future organisational growth.


·      Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement and innovation, leading teams through change and organisational transformation.


About the Ideal Candidate


Qualifications


  • Degree qualification in Business, Operations Management, Public Administration or a related discipline, or significant relevant professional experience - essential


Knowledge


·      Strong understanding of service delivery, operational management, governance and process improvement.

·      Knowledge of digital learning, online learning platforms, learning administration or related service delivery models.


Experience


·      Significant relevant experience leading operational, service delivery or platform-based services at scale, including responsibility for teams, suppliers, budgets and performance outcomes. (essential)

·      Experience managing operational processes, service standards and performance measures to ensure high-quality service delivery. (essential)

·      Experience managing large-scale client-facing services.

·      Experience establishing service standards, performance measures and operational processes.

·      Experience managing suppliers, contracts and service-level performance.

·      Experience managing budgets, expenditure and supporting financial reporting and planning.

·      Experience building effective stakeholder relationships and leading organisational change.


Read more about the ideal candidate profile including the skills and personal attributes, in the candidate booklet.

Conscia will be managing all aspects of the recruitment process on behalf of The IPA. Applications should be made online through https://consciatalent.com/IPA and by attaching a completed application form, downloadable here.

 

Your application must be submitted on the Conscia website not later than 1pm (Irish time) on Wednesday 30th September 2026. Interviews are expected to take place in person, in October.

job.title: Electrical Engineer
job.description:
About IN2 

Formed in 2002, IN2 is a progressive engineering consultancy operating across Ireland, the UK, and Europe, dedicated to creating better spaces for people. With over 100 experts across six locations, our team of engineers, technicians, and consultants collaborate closely with clients and partners to deliver innovative, sustainable, and energy-efficient building solutions across a wide range of sectors—from concept and design through to handover and beyond. 

For over 20 years, we have maintained a people-centric culture that encourages growth, innovation, and adaptability. Our award-winning MEP projects, combined with recognition as a ‘Great Place to Work’, reflect our commitment to quality, sustainability, and a supportive, inclusive work environment where individuals can thrive. 

At IN2, joining our team means being part of a collaborative, high-performing, and forward-thinking organisation, where your contribution makes a real impact—and where career opportunities grow alongside our business. 

 

Working Hours  

We operate a 37.5-hour working week designed to support work-life balance. We offer flexible start and finish times between 8am and 6pm, provided that core hours of 10am to 4pm are covered for team collaboration and meetings.  

 

About The Role 

We are seeking an experienced Electrical Engineer to join our growing Athlone team. This is a permanent position offering an excellent package for the right candidate.  You’ll play a key role in project delivery and receive mentorship from senior engineers to support your career development. 


What you will do 

Athlone offers the chance to do career-defining work without long commutes or city pressure. You will be trusted, supported, and encouraged to shape how things are done locally, with full backing from the wider IN2 team.  As a Senior Electrical Engineer at our Athlone Office, you will:   

  • Assist senior engineers with project management, on-site inspections, technical surveys, and design team meetings 
  • Play an active role in project delivery from concept through to completion 
  • Support the management team in client relationships, budgeting, and reporting 
  • Contribute to mentoring junior staff, reviewing design work, and providing guidance 
  • Collaborate with senior engineers for ongoing mentorship and growth 


Your Experience 

To be considered for this role, you should have:  


Essential 

  • Degree in Building Services Engineering or Electrical Engineering 
  • Minimum of 4 years’ experience in electrical design, ideally within a consultancy environment 
  • Passion for career progression and aspiration to achieve Chartered status (if not already obtained) 


Why You’ll Love Being Part of the Team 

At IN2, we’ve traded the stuffy corporate ladder for a flat hierarchy and a culture where your voice actually matters. We’re a diverse, collaborative team that believes the best ideas can come from anyone, anywhere. 

  • Global Impact, Local Feel: You’ll get to work on game-changing projects across different countries, supported by our specialist BIM, Sustainability, and Building Physics teams. 
  • Constant Growth: Through IN2 Talks, cross-office collaboration, and a culture of knowledge sharing, you’re always learning something new. 
  • Your Best Self: We prioritise a genuine work-life balance with flexible hours and support for personal circumstances. We’re big on open communication and ensuring our workplace is a bias-free zone where you can truly be yourself. 


What’s In It For You? 

We’ve put together a package that looks after your wallet, your career, and your wellbeing. 


The Essentials 

  • Competitive Pay & Bonuses: A salary that reflects your worth, plus an annual bonus and pension contributions. 
  • Annual Leave: 22 days of annual leave, scaling up to 27 days as you grow with us (plus all those bank holidays!). 
  • Flexible Hours: Work-life balance isn't just a buzzword here—we offer a 37.5-hour working week with flexible hours (8am–6pm), to suit your lifestyle! 


Career Progression 

  • Personal Roadmap: You’ll have a dedicated Personal Development Plan and mentoring from our senior leaders. 
  • The IN2 Academy: Access to our internal academy, CPD support, and expert assistance in advancing your career,  

 

Health & Wellbeing 

  • Mind & Body: Access to our Employee Assistance Program, annual health checks, and various fitness initiatives. 
  • Commute Greener: Take advantage of our Cycle to Work scheme to keep active on your way to the office. 


Social & Community 

  • Legendary Events: From our famous Christmas party weekend to Employee Appreciation Day and regular staff social events. 
  • Giving Back: Get involved with our team-led charity initiatives. 
  • International Reach: opportunities to work across IN2 offices in London, Dublin, Berlin, Belfast, Athlone, and Madrid 


Eligibility: Due to regulatory requirements, this role is open to candidates with permanent residency or unrestricted right to work in Ireland only. Applications requiring visa sponsorship cannot be considered.

job.title: Cyber Underwriter
job.description:
Does it ever feel like you’re underwriting with one hand tied behind your back? Tired of the struggles and inefficiencies associated with legacy systems and processes? Spending too much of your time and energy navigating corporate politics? All leaving your efforts to innovate and deliver underwriting excellence languishing?

At Ledgebrook, we believe a career in underwriting can be so much more. You bring the passion and entrepreneurial spirit; we’ll provide the platform to unleash the very best of your talents and skills. Together, we’ll celebrate and reward success! Are you intrigued? Then read on and apply now to advance your career at Ledgebrook.

About the Role

We are seeking experienced Cyber Liability underwriting talent to join our growing team whose mission is focused on building a profitable book of cyber liability business. Our vision is to deliver market relevant solutions to our key wholesale trading partners in a more frictionless environment that places an emphasis on efficiencies and quality to meet or exceed our broker’s overall needs in a risk differentiated manner. If you possess an entrepreneurial passion that includes a proven track history of delivering underwriting excellence and are seeking an opportunity to break out of the traditional insurance company mould, we’re looking for you!

As a member of the Cyber team, you will regularly interact with our wholesale trading partners over the phone, virtually and in-person to drive submission flow and convert on the best opportunities quoted. We are looking for disciplined underwriting candidates that possess a strong overall cyber liability background with experience underwriting risks of all industries and sizes.

We are flexible with both a candidate’s experience level and physical work location. The actual position title (Underwriter, Senior UW, AVP, etc.) will be dependent on a candidate’s specific experience and qualifications. We currently operate in a fully remote work environment, so we’re more focused on your experience and cultural fit than where you physically sit!

About You

Here at Ledgebrook we’re passionate about creating a team that thrives on continuous learning and shares our excitement about building a company from the ground up. We’re looking for people to join us with:

●     A passion for delivering world-class customer service to our internal and external customers

●     Intellectual curiosity and a strong desire for innovation, rather than following the status quo

●     A hunger for continuous learning and opportunities to grow

●     Agile prioritization skills coupled with a keen sense of urgency - we balance getting it right with getting it done right now

●     A strong drive and desire to win together as a high-performing team

●     A moral compass to "do the right thing, period." We have zero tolerance for toxic behaviors

●     An eagerness to actively participate and connect with the whole team, across remote locations

●     An honest, transparent communication style

●     A proactive, solution-oriented mindset. We don’t look for blame, we look for the solution

As a future Cyber Liability Underwriter, your experience and qualifications must include:

●     2+ years experience as a cyber underwriter

●     Experience working in the Cyber E&S market; Tech E&O experience is a plus

●     Ability to work as a team player or independently in a fast-paced work environment

●     Deep wholesale broker trading relationships

●     Effective communication skills to articulate our appetite and develop wholesale broker relationships

●     Understanding of pricing and risk selection criteria to achieve underwriting profit

●     Advanced understanding of data analysis and execution of portfolio management objectives

●     Intellectual curiosity, problem solving skills, and a sense of urgency

●     Responsive, customer service focused mindset and behaviors

●     Ability to make timely decisions with appropriate information and consultation

●     A strong entrepreneurial drive and desire to build and win together as a high performing team

●     Ability to travel to meet with assigned brokers or with the broader team to participate in industry conference or events
